I've been thinking about getting a new mobile workstation so I started browsing the various manufacturers websites to see what they had available. I don't care about thickness or weight as much as durability and expansion options. Anyway, I was severely disappointed by what I found and the prices they were charging. I find it outrageous that an entry-level workstation with mediocre parts and questionable durability is around $2000. I started looking at thin-mini-ITX boards and found that you could have all the essential parts to build your own laptop (with desktop parts) for much less than this, barely over $1000. Combined with a thick, 2-part 3D printed case this would be a mobile beast that you could toss around, and the best part would be the expansion options. Hell, you could put a mechanical keyboard in there, and watercooling is a possibility. I've been working on some models in AutoCAD that would bolt together so the whole thing would be easily assembled / disassembled.

My question is: is anyone else interested in something like this? Obviously I will follow this up with models and parts list over the coming weeks. I could just build one for myself, but the overhead would probably not justify the price vs a Lenovo workstation.

UPDATE 06/11/2016: I'm currently sourcing components for this project. For the first iteration I will be using an embedded Intel Pentium/Celeron thin-ITX motherboard with recycled HP laptop components for prototyping purposes. I'm also developing the CAD models for the shell.

That sounds like an interesting project. I would definitely check it out. A modular laptop that could take a full size pci video card would be pretty cool. Not being able to replace the video card is what keeps me from getting a laptop. What materials are you thinking of using for it?

Materials for the case would mostly be ABS as I think that is the most durable and temperature resistant filament available, attached with regular hardware bolts. I've been toying with the idea of making the lid and bottom out of aluminium or steel sheet which you can order to size online for around $20. I would print the corners and leave a groove so it would accept a standard sized sheet and be replaceable.

I'm not sure how I will work PCI graphics cards yet. A single slot card might be drop in, but likely you'd need to remove the I/O plate and I'm not sure if that means you have to solder on your own connections. The good thing is with how power efficient cards are getting and the ability to switch between dedicated and integrated graphics a desktop card makes perfect sense. Even if you just have it set to only use dedicated when plugged in.

ABS corners with aluminum sides would probably work pretty good and get rid of the heat better than abs. If you only have to print the edges, that is a lot less printing too. You can skip the soldering now, there are 16x pci riser slot extensions from the bitcoin miners you can get for a few bucks that will let you relocate that slot pretty easy. Having that exposed so you can just plug it in when needed is an interesting idea. You could just leave your video card plugged into the tv, and hook the laptop up when you want to use it. Have you tried printing ninjaflex with your machine yet? Its rubber and would help with absorbing shock\vibration.
